title: AI Fieldwork · Standard Exchange

blocks.title: Starting Point
blocks.description: Share what would make an AI feature useful in your work.
blocks.prompt: Which part of an AI feature needs the most attention?

guidedSteps: Choose the response closest to your current experience.
Notice which constraints or perspectives are missing.
Use the group pattern to shape the next discussion.
learningSupport.hint: There is no ideal answer; choose what best matches your team today.
learningSupport.stretchChallenge: Name one piece of evidence that would change your answer.

blocks.title: Grounding Check
blocks.description: Check your understanding of trustworthy AI interactions.

questions.prompt: What should a grounded answer show?
questions.explanation: Sources help people inspect claims; they do not guarantee correctness.

questions.prompt: Where should a user-provided API key live in this app?
questions.explanation: Keep BYOK volatile and out of persistence and realtime messages.

guidedSteps: Read the scenario and identify its main constraint.
Compare each option with the evidence available.
After answering, explain the reasoning to a partner.
learningSupport.hint: Look for the choice that keeps uncertainty visible instead of hiding it.
learningSupport.stretchChallenge: Write a counterexample that would make the chosen answer fail.

blocks.title: Design for Verifiability
blocks.description: A resilient AI experience combines clear constraints, useful citations, fallbacks, and human review.

guidedSteps: Underline the idea that matters most to your work.
Connect it to a recent decision or workflow.
Write one question you would want to verify before acting.
learningSupport.hint: Focus on the smallest useful change, not an idealized end state.
learningSupport.stretchChallenge: Identify a trade-off this principle introduces and how you would monitor it.

blocks.title: 3-Lens Design Lab
blocks.description: Submit one practical contribution from the Experience, Grounding, or Payload lens.

guidedSteps: Experience: describe who needs what and where friction occurs.
Grounding: list the evidence, assumptions, and failure cases.
Payload: identify the minimum data needed and what must stay out.
learningSupport.hint: Start with a specific moment in a real workflow; keep the response focused.
learningSupport.stretchChallenge: Ask someone from another role to challenge one assumption in your design.

blocks.title: Field Testing Sandbox
blocks.description: Try the HKU Lunch Rotator with grounded sources or demo data.

guidedSteps: Set constraints that reflect a real use case.
Inspect sources, coverage, and any missing evidence.
Decide whether the result is ready to test or needs a narrower claim.
learningSupport.hint: Treat generated suggestions as hypotheses; confirm important details independently.
learningSupport.stretchChallenge: Repeat the test with one changed constraint and compare what meaningfully changes.

blocks.title: Field Notes
blocks.description: Capture one experiment to try next and one risk to validate.

guidedSteps: Choose one objective you can apply in your work.
Write an action small enough to try this week.
Name who will notice the result and when you will review it.
learningSupport.hint: A useful next step should fit into an existing workflow.
learningSupport.stretchChallenge: Define a simple signal that would tell you to keep, adapt, or stop the experiment.

learningObjectives: Frame a real work challenge as a testable need for a specific person or team.
Design an AI-assisted workflow that makes evidence and limitations visible.
Plan a small field test with a clear signal and a next review date.
